description_nl: Begrenzing van de 21 Nationale Parken in Nederland. De Nationale Parken zijn grote aaneengesloten natuurgebieden van nationaal en internationaal belang, beheerd door de provincies.
description_en: Boundaries of the 21 National Parks in the Netherlands. National Parks are large contiguous natural areas of national and international importance, managed by the provinces.
license_note: RVO datasets published via PDOK are typically CC0 (public domain). Verify at the PDOK metadata page.
update_frequency: As needed (infrequent — park boundaries change rarely, though 2023-2024 reforms added new parks)

columns.name: bron
columns.description_nl: Bron van de begrenzing — de organisatie die de grens heeft aangeleverd (bijv. provincie, Staatsbosbeheer, Natuurmonumenten)
columns.description_en: Source of the boundary — the organization that supplied the boundary (e.g. province, State Forestry Service, Natuurmonumenten)

columns.name: datum
columns.description_nl: Datum van aanwijzing of vaststelling van het park
columns.description_en: Date of designation or establishment of the park

columns.name: fiat_secr
columns.description_nl: Of de aanwijzing is goedgekeurd door de staatssecretaris (Ja/Nee/leeg)
columns.description_en: Whether the designation was approved by the Secretary of State (Ja=Yes, Nee=No, or blank)

columns.name: hectares
columns.description_nl: Oppervlakte van het park in hectare
columns.description_en: Area of the park in hectares

columns.name: nr
columns.description_en: Sequential number of the park (chronological numbering)

columns.name: objectid
columns.description_en: Internal object ID in the source data

context.what_is_it: The official boundaries of the 21 Nationale Parken (National Parks) of the Netherlands. These are large, contiguous natural areas designated for their ecological, landscape, and recreational value. The dataset is maintained by RVO and published through PDOK. Parks range from coastal dunes (Zuid-Kennemerland, Duinen van Texel) to forests (De Hoge Veluwe, Veluwezoom), wetlands (De Biesbosch, Weerribben-Wieden), heathlands (Dwingelderveld, Sallandse Heuvelrug), and even a tidal estuary (Oosterschelde).
context.why_important: National Parks represent the most important large natural areas in the Netherlands. They serve as anchors for biodiversity conservation, nature-based recreation, and environmental education. Since the 2023 reform, provinces manage the parks with support from the Nationale Parken Bureau, giving parks a stronger governance framework and connecting them to regional spatial planning.
common_uses: Nature conservation planning and spatial analysis
Tourism and recreation planning — park visitor infrastructure
Environmental impact assessment — checking proximity to protected areas
Overlap analysis with Natura 2000 areas and NNN (Natuurnetwerk Nederland)
Land use and landscape change analysis over time

related_datasets.name: Natura 2000
related_datasets.provider: RVO / Ministry of Agriculture, Nature and Food Quality
related_datasets.relationship: EU-level protected nature areas. Many National Parks overlap with Natura 2000 sites, but they are distinct legal designations. Natura 2000 areas are designated under the EU Birds and Habitats Directives.

related_datasets.name: Natuurnetwerk Nederland (NNN)
related_datasets.relationship: The national ecological network. NNN includes all National Parks but is much larger, also covering ecological corridors and development areas. NNN boundaries are set by provinces.

related_datasets.name: Beschermde Natuurmonumenten
related_datasets.relationship: Legally protected nature monuments under the Wet natuurbescherming. Some overlap with National Parks but are a separate legal category.

related_datasets.name: UNESCO World Heritage Sites (Natural)
related_datasets.relationship: The Waddenzee is both a World Heritage Site and borders several National Parks (Schiermonnikoog, Duinen van Texel).

caveats: The dataset has only 21 features — it is a complete enumeration, not a sample.
Some parks have complex multi-polygon boundaries that include water bodies, making area calculations from geometry potentially different from the 'hectares' attribute.
The 'bron' (source) field shows the organization that supplied each boundary; different sources may have used different digitization methods and precision levels.
As of 2024, the system is evolving — the newest park (Van Gogh, nr 22, designated 2024-10-15) demonstrates that new parks can be added.
The oldest parks (Veluwezoom 1930, De Hoge Veluwe 1935) predate the modern National Parks system that was formalized in the 1980s.
One park (Duinen van Texel) has a blank 'fiat_secr' value, meaning it may not have received formal Secretary of State approval.
CRS is EPSG:28992 (Dutch RD New) — reprojection to EPSG:4326 is needed for web mapping and GeoParquet in Portolan.
